papers.title: Prevalence aware feature selection improves biomarker identification in microbiome studies
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Identifying robust microbial biomarkers is crucial for disease diagnosis and prediction, elucidation of biological mechanisms, and development of targeted therapies. Machine learning-based approaches, particularly the random forest model, have been widely used for biomarker identification during sample stratification. However, those biomarkers often vary considerably for the same disease, limiting their practical applicability. A robust framework for reliable biomarker identification in microbiome research is needed. To address this gap, we proposed a prevalence-aware feature selection framework (ParSlet) that incorporates a universal scaling relationship between taxon prevalence and selection frequency. Results We first identified a universal exponential scaling law linking the probability of a taxon being consistently recognized as a biomarker versus its prevalence. Then, we integrated this scaling law with taxa prevalence into the biomarker identification using random forest. We systematically evaluated this approach in both simulated microbiome datasets and real-world microbiome datasets and compared it with existing methods, finding that our integrated approach generally improved feature stability and reproducibility of biomarker identification. In colorectal cancer (CRC) datasets, our method robustly identified well-established microbial biomarkers such as Ruminococcus , Clostridium_XVIII , and Faecalibacterium . Integrating a prevalence-based scaling adjustment into feature importance enhances the stability of microbiome biomarker identification. This approach holds promise for enabling more reliable disease diagnostics, uncovering generalizable microbial signatures across cohorts, and guiding the development of targeted microbiome-based interventions. Availability ParSlet is available at https://github.com/KelabatOSU/Feature_selection

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
在疾病诊断与预测、生物机制研究以及靶向疗法的开发中，识别可靠的微生物生物标志物至关重要。基于机器学习的方法，尤其是随机森林模型，在样本分层分析中已被广泛用于生物标志物的筛选。然而，对于同一种疾病而言，这些生物标志物的稳定性往往存在显著差异，从而限制了它们的实际应用价值。因此，亟需建立一个稳健的框架来确保微生物组研究中生物标志物的可靠识别。为解决这一问题，我们提出了一种基于物种丰度特征的筛选方法——ParSlet，该方法充分考虑了物种丰度与其被选为生物标志物的频率之间的普遍关联规律。  

**研究结果**  
首先，我们发现了一个普遍存在的指数级缩放关系：某种物种被持续识别为生物标志物的概率与其丰度之间存在正相关关系。随后，我们将这一缩放规律融入随机森林模型中，用于生物标志物的筛选。通过在模拟微生物组数据集及真实世界微生物组数据集中进行系统测试，并与现有方法进行比较，我们发现这种整合方法显著提升了生物标志物识别的稳定性与重复性。在结直肠癌数据集中，我们的方法成功识别出了Ruminococcus、Clostridium_XVIII和Faecalibacterium等公认的微生物生物标志物。将基于丰度的缩放调整机制纳入特征重要性评估体系中，确实能够增强微生物组生物标志物识别的可靠性。这一方法有望为更准确的疾病诊断提供支持，揭示不同人群中具有普遍意义的微生物特征，并为针对微生物组的干预措施的研发提供重要依据。  

**开源信息**  
ParSlet工具已公开发布在以下链接：https://github.com/KelabatOSU/Feature_selection

首先，我们发现了一个描述物种被持续识别为生物标志物的概率与其丰度之间关系的通用指数级缩放规律；随后，我们将这一规律融入随机森林模型中，用于生物标志物的识别。我们在模拟的微生物组数据集及真实的微生物组数据集中系统地验证了这一方法，并将其与现有方法进行了比较。结果表明，我们的方法显著提升了生物标志物识别的稳定性与重复性。在结直肠癌数据集中，该方法能够准确识别出Ruminococcus、Clostridium_XVIII和Faecalibacterium等公认的微生物生物标志物。将基于物种丰度的缩放调整机制纳入特征重要性评估体系中，确实增强了微生物组生物标志物识别的可靠性。这一方法有望为更准确的疾病诊断提供支持，揭示不同人群中具有普遍意义的微生物特征，并为针对微生物组的干预措施的研发提供指导。

papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: Identifying robust microbial biomarkers is crucial for disease diagnosis and prediction, elucidation of biological mechanisms, and development of targeted therapies. Machine learning-based approaches, particularly the random forest model, have been widely used for biomarker identification during sample stratification. However, those biomarkers often vary considerably for the same disease, limiting their practical applicability. A robust framework for reliable biomarker identification in microbiome research is needed. To address this gap, we proposed a prevalence-aware feature selection framework (ParSlet) that incorporates a universal scaling relationship between taxon prevalence and selection frequency.

RESULTS: We first identified a universal exponential scaling law linking the probability of a taxon being consistently recognized as a biomarker versus its prevalence. Then, we integrated this scaling law with taxa prevalence into the biomarker identification using random forest. We systematically evaluated this approach in both simulated microbiome datasets and real-world microbiome datasets and compared it with existing methods, finding that our integrated approach generally improved feature stability and reproducibility of biomarker identification. In colorectal cancer (CRC) datasets, our method robustly identified well-established microbial biomarkers such as Ruminococcus, Clostridium_XVIII, and Faecalibacterium. Integrating a prevalence-based scaling adjustment into feature importance enhances the stability of microbiome biomarker identification. This approach holds promise for enabling more reliable disease diagnostics, uncovering generalizable microbial signatures across cohorts, and guiding the development of targeted microbiome-based interventions.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

papers.title: Inferring Dynamic Information from Protein Structures by Gaussian Integrals and Deep Learning
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Protein dynamics are central to function, but experiments and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations remain costly, low-throughput, and difficult to compare across protocols. Scalable structure-based methods are needed to infer dynamics from static protein structures. Results We present a deep learning framework that predicts protein dynamics from 30-dimensional Gaussian integral (GI) descriptors of Cα backbone topology. Using 1,374 ATLAS protein chains with MD-derived RMSF, GI stratified proteins into fold-relevant clusters enriched for secondary structure, sequence homology, and ECOD families. An attention-based 1D-CNN classified flexible versus non-flexible proteins with test AUC = 0.772 and separated slow-mode– from fast-mode–dominated dynamics with AUC = 0.91. Regression models recovered mean RMSF (Pearson r = 0.72; R² = 0.46) and slow-mode RMSF more accurately (Pearson r = 0.83; R² = 0.62), supporting rapid inference of flexibility and collective-motion bias. Availability and implementation Code and data are available on GitHub at: https://github.com/fvilicich/gaussian_integral/blob/main/gaussian_integral_classification.ipynb

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
蛋白质的动力学特性对其功能至关重要，然而现有的实验方法及分子动力学模拟不仅成本高昂、效率低下，而且不同研究方案之间的结果也难以进行直接比较。因此，亟需开发基于结构信息的可扩展方法，以便从静态的蛋白质结构中推断其动态行为。  

**研究结果**  
我们构建了一个深度学习框架，该框架能够利用30维的高斯积分描述符来预测蛋白质的动力学特性。通过对1,374条ATLAS蛋白链的数据进行分析，这些数据包含了通过分子动力学计算得到的RMSF值，我们发现高斯积分描述符能够将蛋白质按照其折叠结构、二级结构特征以及所属的ECOD分类进行有效分组。基于注意力机制的一维卷积神经网络在区分蛋白质的柔韧性方面表现出优异的性能，测试AUC值为0.772；同时，该模型也能准确区分以慢速运动模式为主还是快速运动模式为主的蛋白质动态行为，其分离准确率高达0.91。回归分析进一步证实，这些机器学习模型能够较为准确地预测蛋白质的平均RMSF值（Pearson r = 0.72; R² = 0.46）以及以慢速运动模式为主的蛋白质的RMSF值（Pearson r = 0.83; R² = 0.62），从而为快速评估蛋白质的柔韧性及其集体运动特性提供了有力支持。

papers.title: Hotgenes: an R package for reducing bottlenecks in bulk omics data exploration and collaboration
papers.summary: Abstract Summary A critical part of omics analysis is the transition from early data exploration to final interpretation, often including different analytical platforms and the proliferation of figures, tables, and files. To minimize potential errors and delays that can occur during this process, we have developed an R package called “Hotgenes” that contains a wide range of flexible utilities available in a single modular Shiny application. With Hotgenes, differential expression results generated from bulk omics platforms can be imported and shared among collaborators with minimal coding. Furthermore, the modular Hotgenes user interface can be customized by advanced users to fit the needs of their evolving pipelines. Availability and Implementation Hotgenes is implemented in R and is freely available at https://github.com/pfizer-opensource/Open-Hotgenes . A permanent archived version is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20129460

**摘要**  
经福尔马林固定、石蜡包埋处理的组织在临床与研究领域被广泛使用，但这类样本在进行RNA测序时，由于胞嘧啶脱氨作用及链特异性损伤会导致人工突变的出现，从而影响体细胞突变的检测效果。现有的用于去除这些噪声的工具都是为DNA测序设计的，且依赖于序列链的偏倚性，因此并不适用于RNA测序。本文提出的FFixR是一种基于机器学习的工具，它能够在无需匹配正常样本的情况下，有效清除RNA测序数据中由福尔马林固定处理引起的伪突变。  

**研究结果**  
通过在含有匹配DNA样本的黑色素瘤组织上进行训练，FFixR能够利用等位基因特异性读数、变异特征以及突变特征概率来识别真实突变。实验结果显示，该工具可去除高达98%的伪突变，同时仍能保持约92%的真实突变检出率。SHAP分析进一步揭示了影响模型决策的关键因素。当将该工具应用于其他独立样本集时，它成功恢复了RNA与DNA测序结果所反映的肿瘤突变负担之间的相关性（R²=0.881），并准确识别出了具有生物学意义的突变特征。FFixR的出现为利用福尔马林固定组织进行RNA测序提供了有力支持，极大地扩展了这类存档样本在科研与临床应用中的价值。  

**工具获取与使用方式**  
FFixR工具可免费在以下网址下载：  
https://github.com/yizhak-lab-ccg/FFixR  
https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31998315

papers.title: DruGUI 2.0: Mapping Protein Druggability with Probe-Based Molecular Dynamics
papers.summary: Abstract Summary We introduce DruGUI 2.0, a drug discovery tool for assessing the druggability of proteins, integrated into the ProDy application programming interface (API). DruGUI 2.0 is developed to facilitate the search for druggable sites while allowing for proteins’ conformational flexibility. Simulations in explicit solvent, with an option to include membrane, are carried out in the presence of probe molecules selected from an expanded library of small molecules containing drug-like fragments. Druggable sites beyond orthosteric sites are identifiable, as well as the probes that show high affinity to bind to those sites. Characterization of the composition and position of the probes helps build pharmacophore models and estimate relative binding affinities. As a Python module with enhanced visualization features, DruGUI 2.0 complements, and benefits from, the vast collection of protein sequence, structure, and dynamics analyses modules accessible in ProDy . Case studies in the Supplemental Material showcase the utility of DruGUI 2.0 applied to both soluble targets and membrane proteins. Availability ProDy is open-sourced and freely available under MIT License from https://github.com/prody/ProDy . The code version of DruGUI 2.0 used for simulations is available on Zenodo : 10.5281/zenodo.20511357

papers.primary_summary_raw:
SUMMARY: We introduce DruGUI 2.0, a drug discovery tool for assessing the druggability of proteins, integrated into the ProDy application programming interface (API). DruGUI 2.0 is developed to facilitate the search for druggable sites while allowing for proteins' conformational flexibility. Simulations in explicit solvent, with an option to include membrane, are carried out in the presence of probe molecules selected from an expanded library of small molecules containing drug-like fragments. Druggable sites beyond orthosteric sites are identifiable, as well as the probes that show high affinity to bind to those sites. Characterization of the composition and position of the probes helps build pharmacophore models and estimate relative binding affinities. As a Python module with enhanced visualization features, DruGUI 2.0 complements, and benefits from, the vast collection of protein sequence, structure, and dynamics analyses modules accessible in ProDy. Case studies in the Supplemental Material showcase the utility of DruGUI 2.0 applied to both soluble targets and membrane proteins.

AVAILABILITY: ProDy is open-sourced and freely available under MIT License from https://github.com/prody/ProDy. The code version of DruGUI 2.0 used for simulations is available on Zenodo : 10.5281/zenodo.20511357.

all_papers.title: Prevalence aware feature selection improves biomarker identification in microbiome studies
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Identifying robust microbial biomarkers is crucial for disease diagnosis and prediction, elucidation of biological mechanisms, and development of targeted therapies. Machine learning-based approaches, particularly the random forest model, have been widely used for biomarker identification during sample stratification. However, those biomarkers often vary considerably for the same disease, limiting their practical applicability. A robust framework for reliable biomarker identification in microbiome research is needed. To address this gap, we proposed a prevalence-aware feature selection framework (ParSlet) that incorporates a universal scaling relationship between taxon prevalence and selection frequency. Results We first identified a universal exponential scaling law linking the probability of a taxon being consistently recognized as a biomarker versus its prevalence. Then, we integrated this scaling law with taxa prevalence into the biomarker identification using random forest. We systematically evaluated this approach in both simulated microbiome datasets and real-world microbiome datasets and compared it with existing methods, finding that our integrated approach generally improved feature stability and reproducibility of biomarker identification. In colorectal cancer (CRC) datasets, our method robustly identified well-established microbial biomarkers such as Ruminococcus , Clostridium_XVIII , and Faecalibacterium . Integrating a prevalence-based scaling adjustment into feature importance enhances the stability of microbiome biomarker identification. This approach holds promise for enabling more reliable disease diagnostics, uncovering generalizable microbial signatures across cohorts, and guiding the development of targeted microbiome-based interventions. Availability ParSlet is available at https://github.com/KelabatOSU/Feature_selection

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
在疾病诊断与预测、生物机制研究以及靶向疗法的开发中，识别可靠的微生物生物标志物至关重要。基于机器学习的方法，尤其是随机森林模型，在样本分层分析中已被广泛用于生物标志物的筛选。然而，对于同一种疾病而言，这些生物标志物的稳定性往往存在显著差异，从而限制了它们的实际应用价值。因此，亟需建立一个稳健的框架来确保微生物组研究中生物标志物的可靠识别。为解决这一问题，我们提出了一种基于物种丰度特征的筛选方法——ParSlet，该方法充分考虑了物种丰度与其被选为生物标志物的频率之间的普遍关联规律。  

**研究结果**  
首先，我们发现了一个普遍存在的指数级缩放关系：某种物种被持续识别为生物标志物的概率与其丰度之间存在正相关关系。随后，我们将这一缩放规律融入随机森林模型中，用于生物标志物的筛选。通过在模拟微生物组数据集及真实世界微生物组数据集中进行系统测试，并与现有方法进行比较，我们发现这种整合方法显著提升了生物标志物识别的稳定性与重复性。在结直肠癌数据集中，我们的方法成功识别出了Ruminococcus、Clostridium_XVIII和Faecalibacterium等公认的微生物生物标志物。将基于丰度的缩放调整机制纳入特征重要性评估体系中，确实能够增强微生物组生物标志物识别的可靠性。这一方法有望为更准确的疾病诊断提供支持，揭示不同人群中具有普遍意义的微生物特征，并为针对微生物组的干预措施的研发提供重要依据。  

**开源信息**  
ParSlet工具已公开发布在以下链接：https://github.com/KelabatOSU/Feature_selection

all_papers.title: Inferring Dynamic Information from Protein Structures by Gaussian Integrals and Deep Learning
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Protein dynamics are central to function, but experiments and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations remain costly, low-throughput, and difficult to compare across protocols. Scalable structure-based methods are needed to infer dynamics from static protein structures. Results We present a deep learning framework that predicts protein dynamics from 30-dimensional Gaussian integral (GI) descriptors of Cα backbone topology. Using 1,374 ATLAS protein chains with MD-derived RMSF, GI stratified proteins into fold-relevant clusters enriched for secondary structure, sequence homology, and ECOD families. An attention-based 1D-CNN classified flexible versus non-flexible proteins with test AUC = 0.772 and separated slow-mode– from fast-mode–dominated dynamics with AUC = 0.91. Regression models recovered mean RMSF (Pearson r = 0.72; R² = 0.46) and slow-mode RMSF more accurately (Pearson r = 0.83; R² = 0.62), supporting rapid inference of flexibility and collective-motion bias. Availability and implementation Code and data are available on GitHub at: https://github.com/fvilicich/gaussian_integral/blob/main/gaussian_integral_classification.ipynb

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
蛋白质的动力学特性对其功能至关重要，然而现有的实验方法及分子动力学模拟不仅成本高昂、效率低下，而且不同研究方案之间的结果也难以进行直接比较。因此，亟需开发基于结构信息的可扩展方法，以便从静态的蛋白质结构中推断其动态行为。  

**研究结果**  
我们构建了一个深度学习框架，该框架能够利用30维的高斯积分描述符来预测蛋白质的动力学特性。通过对1,374条ATLAS蛋白链的数据进行分析，这些数据包含了通过分子动力学计算得到的RMSF值，我们发现高斯积分描述符能够将蛋白质按照其折叠结构、二级结构特征以及所属的ECOD分类进行有效分组。基于注意力机制的一维卷积神经网络在区分蛋白质的柔韧性方面表现出优异的性能，测试AUC值为0.772；同时，该模型也能准确区分以慢速运动模式为主还是快速运动模式为主的蛋白质动态行为，其分离准确率高达0.91。回归分析进一步证实，这些机器学习模型能够较为准确地预测蛋白质的平均RMSF值（Pearson r = 0.72; R² = 0.46）以及以慢速运动模式为主的蛋白质的RMSF值（Pearson r = 0.83; R² = 0.62），从而为快速评估蛋白质的柔韧性及其集体运动特性提供了有力支持。

https://github.com/fvilicich/gaussianintegral/blob/main/gaussian_integral_classification.ipynb

all_papers.title: Hotgenes: an R package for reducing bottlenecks in bulk omics data exploration and collaboration
all_papers.summary: Abstract Summary A critical part of omics analysis is the transition from early data exploration to final interpretation, often including different analytical platforms and the proliferation of figures, tables, and files. To minimize potential errors and delays that can occur during this process, we have developed an R package called “Hotgenes” that contains a wide range of flexible utilities available in a single modular Shiny application. With Hotgenes, differential expression results generated from bulk omics platforms can be imported and shared among collaborators with minimal coding. Furthermore, the modular Hotgenes user interface can be customized by advanced users to fit the needs of their evolving pipelines. Availability and Implementation Hotgenes is implemented in R and is freely available at https://github.com/pfizer-opensource/Open-Hotgenes . A permanent archived version is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20129460

all_papers.title: FFixR: A Machine Learning Framework for Accurate Somatic Mutation Calling from FFPE RNA-Seq Data in Cancer
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues are widely used in clinical and research settings, yet their use for detecting somatic mutations from RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) is hindered by artefactual mutations introduced by cytosine deamination and strand-specific damage. Existing FFPE noise-filtering tools are tailored to DNA-seq and rely on strand bias, rendering them unsuitable for RNA-seq. Here, we present FFixR, a machine learning–based framework that filters FFPE-induced artefacts from RNA-seq data without requiring matched-normal samples. Results Trained on FFPE melanoma samples with matched DNA, FFixR leverages allele-specific read counts, variant features, and mutational signature probabilities. FFixR removed up to 98% of artefactual mutations while maintaining ∼92% recall of true variants. SHAP analysis revealed key feature interactions guiding model decisions. When applied to independent cohorts, FFixR restored the correlation between RNA- and DNA-derived tumor mutational burden (R 2 = 0.881) and recovered biologically meaningful mutational signatures. FFixR enables accurate somatic variant calling from FFPE RNA-seq data, expanding the utility of archival samples for research and clinical applications. Availability and implementation FFixR tool is freely available on the web at https://github.com/yizhak-lab-ccg/FFixR and https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31998315 . The repository also includes a readme file describing the inputs, outputs and the entire pipeline. The results presented here were produced using v1.0.0

经福尔马林固定、石蜡包埋处理的组织在临床与研究领域被广泛使用，但这类样本在进行RNA测序时，由于胞嘧啶脱氨作用及链特异性损伤会导致人工突变的出现，从而影响体细胞突变的检测效果。现有的用于去除这些噪声的工具都是为DNA测序设计的，且依赖于序列链的偏倚性，因此并不适用于RNA测序。本文提出的FFixR是一种基于机器学习的工具，它能够在无需匹配正常样本的情况下，有效清除RNA测序数据中由福尔马林固定处理引起的伪突变。  

**研究结果**  
通过在含有匹配DNA样本的黑色素瘤组织上进行训练，FFixR能够利用等位基因特异性读数、变异特征以及突变特征概率来识别真实突变。实验结果显示，该工具可去除高达98%的伪突变，同时仍能保持约92%的真实突变检出率。SHAP分析进一步揭示了影响模型决策的关键因素。当将该工具应用于其他独立样本集时，它成功恢复了RNA与DNA测序结果所反映的肿瘤突变负担之间的相关性（R²=0.881），并准确识别出了具有生物学意义的突变特征。FFixR的出现为利用福尔马林固定组织进行RNA测序提供了有力支持，极大地扩展了这类存档样本在科研与临床应用中的价值。  

**工具获取与使用方式**  
FFixR工具可免费在以下网址下载：  
https://github.com/yizhak-lab-ccg/FFixR  
https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31998315  
该代码库中还提供了详细的文档，说明输入数据格式、输出结果以及整个处理流程。本研究所使用的FFixR版本为v1.0.0。

all_papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues are widely used in clinical and research settings, yet their use for detecting somatic mutations from RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) is hindered by artefactual mutations introduced by cytosine deamination and strand-specific damage. Existing FFPE noise-filtering tools are tailored to DNA-seq and rely on strand bias, rendering them unsuitable for RNA-seq. Here, we present FFixR, a machine learning-based framework that filters FFPE-induced artefacts from RNA-seq data without requiring matched-normal samples.

RESULTS: Trained on FFPE melanoma samples with matched DNA, FFixR leverages allele-specific read counts, variant features, and mutational signature probabilities. FFixR removed up to 98% of artefactual mutations while maintaining ∼92% recall of true variants. SHAP analysis revealed key feature interactions guiding model decisions. When applied to independent cohorts, FFixR restored the correlation between RNA- and DNA-derived tumor mutational burden (R2 = 0.881) and recovered biologically meaningful mutational signatures. FFixR enables accurate somatic variant calling from FFPE RNA-seq data, expanding the utility of archival samples for research and clinical applications.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: FFixR tool is freely available on the web at https://github.com/yizhak-lab-ccg/FFixR and https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31998315. The repository also includes a readme file describing the inputs, outputs and the entire pipeline. The results presented here were produced using v1.0.0.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

all_papers.title: DruGUI 2.0: Mapping Protein Druggability with Probe-Based Molecular Dynamics
all_papers.summary: Abstract Summary We introduce DruGUI 2.0, a drug discovery tool for assessing the druggability of proteins, integrated into the ProDy application programming interface (API). DruGUI 2.0 is developed to facilitate the search for druggable sites while allowing for proteins’ conformational flexibility. Simulations in explicit solvent, with an option to include membrane, are carried out in the presence of probe molecules selected from an expanded library of small molecules containing drug-like fragments. Druggable sites beyond orthosteric sites are identifiable, as well as the probes that show high affinity to bind to those sites. Characterization of the composition and position of the probes helps build pharmacophore models and estimate relative binding affinities. As a Python module with enhanced visualization features, DruGUI 2.0 complements, and benefits from, the vast collection of protein sequence, structure, and dynamics analyses modules accessible in ProDy . Case studies in the Supplemental Material showcase the utility of DruGUI 2.0 applied to both soluble targets and membrane proteins. Availability ProDy is open-sourced and freely available under MIT License from https://github.com/prody/ProDy . The code version of DruGUI 2.0 used for simulations is available on Zenodo : 10.5281/zenodo.20511357

all_papers.primary_summary_raw:
SUMMARY: We introduce DruGUI 2.0, a drug discovery tool for assessing the druggability of proteins, integrated into the ProDy application programming interface (API). DruGUI 2.0 is developed to facilitate the search for druggable sites while allowing for proteins' conformational flexibility. Simulations in explicit solvent, with an option to include membrane, are carried out in the presence of probe molecules selected from an expanded library of small molecules containing drug-like fragments. Druggable sites beyond orthosteric sites are identifiable, as well as the probes that show high affinity to bind to those sites. Characterization of the composition and position of the probes helps build pharmacophore models and estimate relative binding affinities. As a Python module with enhanced visualization features, DruGUI 2.0 complements, and benefits from, the vast collection of protein sequence, structure, and dynamics analyses modules accessible in ProDy. Case studies in the Supplemental Material showcase the utility of DruGUI 2.0 applied to both soluble targets and membrane proteins.

AVAILABILITY: ProDy is open-sourced and freely available under MIT License from https://github.com/prody/ProDy. The code version of DruGUI 2.0 used for simulations is available on Zenodo : 10.5281/zenodo.20511357.
